title: Reconcile recycled stream IDs in multiplexed connections to prevent cross-tenant usage misattribution
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: In high-throughput multiplexed websocket/HTTP2 connections we have observed cases where clients reuse or recycle stream/request identifiers (stream IDs, request tags) on long-lived TCP connections. Our metering pipeline currently attributes token/response usage by matching per-frame metadata to the last-seen request id -> account mapping. When a client reuses an ID for a new request that is semantically owned by a different customer or sub-account (common in proxy / pooled-client libraries), the pipeline can incorrectly credit the previous account or create orphaned ledger entries. This manifests as short-lived mischarges, blurred quotas, and incorrect per-customer dashboards.

Scope: Fix attribution for multiplexed flows originating from shared sockets and pooled HTTP/2 or websocket clients. Targeted protocols: Redwood streaming websocket API and HTTP/2 server push/multiplexed flows. Does not include: single-request REST flows or dedicated per-connection tenancy tables (already correct).

Why now: We saw customer reports and billing audit spikes during a recent load test with a proxy that pooled connections across sub-accounts. This issue can lead to medium-high financial/operational impact and undermines tenant isolation guarantees.

Non-goals: Rewriting client libraries, changing public API. We aim to make server-side attribution robust to client reuse patterns.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Run a local HTTP/2 client that opens a single connection and issues requests with stream IDs reused in quick succession across different 'X-Client-Account' headers.
2) Observe server frames: the pipeline assigns streaming frames to the original account that established the stream ID rather than the account header on the new request.
3) Reproduce on staging with connection pooling enabled and multiple sub-accounts multiplexed onto the same socket to see cross-account ledger entries in the metering audit logs.
proposed_solution: 1) Introduce a short-lived association epoch for (connection_id, stream_id) tuples backed by an explicit request-start event. The epoch flips only after we observe an explicit request-start marker or a safe timeout + explicit framing boundary.

2) Require authoritative account binding from the first non-heartbeat frame of a request. If a reused stream_id appears with a different account header, treat it as a new epoch only after we validate a request-start frame sequence (prevents mid-stream hijack attribution).

3) Add a reconciliation pass in the metering pipeline: retroactively reconcile orphaned frames if their new epoch maps to a different account and adjust the ledgers with a compensating entry (preserve idempotency).
4) Emit a high-cardinality metric and audit log whenever stream_id reuse across accounts is detected so SRE/Support can triage and notify customers.
5) Backfill existing staging logs to quantify frequency and build a regression test in the e2e harness that simulates pooled client behavior.
tradeoffs_and_risks: - Introducing an epoch/timestamp adds state to the connection demuxer; must be bounded to avoid memory growth on long-lived connections.

- Conservative validation (requiring explicit request-start) may temporarily delay attribution for edge-case clients that send metadata out-of-band; we will provide a short grace period and a togglegable compatibility mode.
- Retroactive reconciliation must be careful to avoid double-charging; compensation entries must be audit-friendly and idempotent.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature branch: implement in demuxer + metering worker with feature flag 'recycled-stream-protection' (can be enabled per-cluster).
2) Canary: enable on internal staging and 5% of low-risk customer traffic; monitor audit anomalies and billing diffs.
3) Gradual ramp: 25% -> 75% -> 100% over two weeks if no U/X or billing regressions seen.
4) Post-deploy: 72-hour intensive monitoring window and a rollback plan to disable the feature flag if unexpected behavior is seen.
acceptance_criteria: - No cross-account ledger attributions created during PoC reproducible scenario in staging (deterministic test passes).
- Reconciliation path produces at most one compensating ledger entry per affected frame and final ledgers match ground-truth from test harness.
- Metrics: detection metric fired on test vectors; alerting rate below threshold on production canary.
- Monitor: per-customer billing discrepancies reduced to zero for reproduced cases and no regression in overall token tallies.
